plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Others will bid their values, so if I win I pay the second-highest value. Overbidding risks negative profit; underbidding risks losing when I should win. There’s no informative history and only one round, so no learning adjustment. Tie-breaking randomness doesn’t change optimality of truth-telling. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 40.

[ This is a one-shot, independent private values, second-price auction with rational opponents. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies, because if you win you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Any shading risks losing when winning would have been profitable, and overbidding risks negative profit if you beat someone above your value. With value $13 and $0.1 increments, bid exactly 13.0. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding 17 ensures we win exactly when our value exceeds both others and we pay the second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative surplus equal to 17 minus the next-highest bid. Shading down risks losing profitable wins; shading up risks winning at a loss if the second-highest exceeds 17. Single round, no strategic dynamics to exploit. ]
